_what_this_measures: Crash resistance, media survival and source integrity across many repeated scans. Accuracy is a separate gate with its own locked evaluation set. Conflating them is what made this one unpassable: two of its three fixtures were being graded against expectations that could not apply to them.
_fixture_paths: Expanded with ~ and environment variables, so a fixture can live in the Mimir library rather than on a removable drive. The two required fixtures used to be absolute paths on D:, which left this gate unrunnable whenever the stick was unplugged -- the normal state of a USB stick, and it had already killed one experiment run partway through.
_source_set: Present only where the footage is the complete, pinned set the labels in benchmark_labels.csv were written against. Omitted means scan-only: the fixture is real footage worth scanning 500 times, but grading it would be grading a subset against labels for the whole.

fixtures.name: library_person_near_partial
fixtures.notes: Scan-only. Holds the 12-43-26 group but not 12-44-29, so it covers one of the two known_person_near_set labels. Verified separately on the detector-enabled path: 12-43-26 resolves REVIEW as labelled. The pinned accuracy fixture stays in benchmark_suite.json.

fixtures.name: library_multi_camera_grouping
fixtures.notes: Scan-only, four camera angles. Nothing in benchmark_labels.csv covers it.

scenarios.name: no_object_detection
scenarios.notes: Without the detector the pipeline escalates on purpose, to stay safe rather than silently miss a collision. Every label is written for the detector-enabled path, so a hard negative graded here fails by design. What this scenario is for is proving the fallback does not crash.
